label: OnBuy
terms_note: OnBuy seller account (UK); consumer key + secret from the seller dashboard; bearer request-token with expiry; rate limits apply (numbers not on the overview); sandbox api-test.onbuy.com.

discovery.auth: token (consumer key + secret key from the seller dashboard → request-token bearer with expiry)

reference.verdict: **Verdict** — has_api: **yes**.Confidence: **high** — official developer documentation opened by the auditor.
auth: 1. Seller dashboard → API credentials (consumer key + secret key).
2. POST auth/request-token → bearer token with expiry; refresh before expiry.
3. Bearer on every call; site_id (UK) as parameter.

endpoints.purpose: create listing on an OPC; update price / stock
create products when no OPC exists

reference.limits: Rate limiting applies (overview); numbers not read. - OnBuy seller terms; keys are the seller's own.
mcp_sdk: none official found in the pages opened

fields.name: consumer_key
fields.help: Consumer key from the OnBuy/OnCommerce Seller Control Panel > Integrations > OnBuy API (Test and Live keys differ).

fields.name: secret_key
fields.help: Secret key from the same page; exchanged with the consumer key at POST /v2/auth/request-token for a 15-minute access token (bound to the calling IP), sent as the raw Authorization header.

config_fields.name: site_id
config_fields.help: OnBuy site id your listings/orders belong to: 2000 = OnBuy UK (GET /v2/sites lists the others).

adapter.terms: OnBuy (OnCommerce) API v2: hourly and daily limits per request method; access tokens last 15 minutes and are tied to the requesting IP. Listing updates are recommended in batches (up to 1000 SKUs) to stay within limits.

me.note: No seller-profile call without the seller id; the probe obtains a token (verifying the consumer/secret keys) and reads the configured site.

update_listing.note: Product Listings: Update by SKU — PUT /v2/listings/by-sku {site_id, listings: [{sku, price, stock}]} changes the LIVE price and/or stock of your listing; `listing_id` is your SKU. Per-SKU problems come back in results[].error (e.g. 'SKU does not exist') with HTTP 200 — check raw/error. Title/description belong to the product (OPC) and are not changed here.

set_inventory.note: Update by SKU with {sku, stock}: sets the stock of one listing (`sku` required). Per-SKU errors are returned in results[].error with HTTP 200.

end_listing.note: Product Listings: Delete by SKU — DELETE /v2/listings/by-sku {site_id, skus: [sku]} DELETES your listing (the product/OPC remains; re-listing needs a new create). `listing_id` is your SKU; the per-SKU outcome ({status: ok} or {error}) is in raw.results.

list_orders.note: Orders: Browse — filter[status] awaiting_dispatch (the default when omitted) | dispatched | partially_dispatched | cancelled | cancelled_by_seller | cancelled_by_buyer | refunded | partially_refunded | all; since = filter[date_from] as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'. price_total is a decimal string; buyer, addresses and products are in raw. No page parameters are documented, so only the first result page is returned.

mark_shipped.note: Orders: Dispatch — PUT /v2/orders/dispatch {site_id, orders: [{order_id, tracking: {supplier_name, number}}]} marks the WHOLE order dispatched and e-mails the buyer. supplier_name (`carrier`) is required whenever a tracking number is sent and is for internal reference only (OnBuy detects the courier from the number). Per-order success/failure is in raw.results[order_id].

not_offered.create_listing: Listings are created on an existing OnBuy product: POST /v2/products/{opc}/listings needs the product's OPC code (or a product must first be created with category, brand and technical details via POST /v2/products); the vocabulary has no OPC or category.

evidence: host api.onbuy.com: DNS ok, TLSv1.3 (Sectigo Limited)
probe: 6/6 tools answered on their documented path with an auth refusal, a validation error or data; control route -> 404 (not_found), so the answers are path-specific
HTML docs spot-check (render-doc): 3/6 tool paths found verbatim on their docs pages; names not found on the page: end_listing:skus
